_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every `contains` marker is still present and every `not_contains` marker is still absent, failing CI if a reprint regressed one.

handfixes.summary: Stripped object sub-selections from association/enum fields in queries.go - the live SuperOps schema returns them as scalar leaf types (JSON/String), so the `{ ... }` sub-selections caused SubSelectionNotAllowed on every typed list/get command (issue #114, reported by @AvlCompCo).
handfixes.why: The CLI was minted from published docs without live introspection (auth-gated → HTTP 400); the queries.go header literally warned VERIFY-ON-FIRST-USE. The source spec.yaml declared every association field `type: string` (→ a scalar Go struct field in internal/types) yet ALSO carried a `selection:` key, so the generator emitted a sub-selection that contradicts its own scalar output contract. All 46 such fields across 18 entities are scalar in internal/types, so the bare-scalar form is the only consistent shape. A full reprint re-runs the generator against the un-fixed spec.yaml and would re-introduce the bug. The not_contains markers below ban each buggy shape; queries_issue114_test.go is the behavioral guard.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press source spec.yaml (~/printing-press/library/superops/spec.yaml, types: section), remove the `selection:` key from every association/enum field (status, priority, client, site, requester, technician, techGroup, sla, accountManager, primaryContact, hqSite, asset, category, designation, role, team, ticket). They are JSON/String scalars, not objects. Done on the press copy 2026-06-16; re-confirm before any reprint.

handfixes.summary: Restored the Subdomain + Region config support in internal/config/config.go that the printing-press 4.24.0 reprint (superops-v0.1.2) silently dropped. Without it the CLI never sends the CustomerSubDomain header, so SuperOps' nginx ingress rejects every GraphQL request with HTTP 400 (empty body) before it reaches the app - all API connectivity broke vs v0.1.0 (issue #132, reported by @AvlCompCo).
handfixes.why: SuperOps' MSP API scopes every request to a tenant via the CustomerSubDomain header and routes EU tenants to euapi.superops.ai. v0.1.0 carried this in config.go (SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN -> Headers[CustomerSubDomain]; SUPEROPS_REGION=eu -> euapi base URL). The spec.yaml does not encode it, so a full reprint regenerates config.go from the spec and re-drops it. The docs (README/SKILL/guide/governance/page.json) still document SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN/SUPEROPS_REGION and promise the header, which masked the drop. The contains markers below pin the restored code; config_issue132_test.go is the behavioral guard (header present on env+file subdomain, EU base-URL switch, explicit base-URL override still wins).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: In the press source spec.yaml (~/printing-press/library/superops/spec.yaml), declare SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN and SUPEROPS_REGION as user_config env vars and encode the request-header mapping (subdomain -> CustomerSubDomain) + EU region base-URL routing so a reprint regenerates config.go with this logic instead of dropping it. NOT yet applied to the press copy as of 2026-06-17 (the v0.1.0 logic was hand-added, not spec-derived); until then, re-apply this hand-fix after any reprint. The asserts below fail CI if a reprint regresses it.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For superops the manifest gained: SUPEROPS_BASE_URL, SUPEROPS_REGION, SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN. server.json gained: SUPEROPS_BASE_URL, SUPEROPS_REGION, SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: SUPEROPS_BASE_URL, SUPEROPS_REGION, SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: An MCP tool call can no longer name a file or directory on the MCP host: the cobratree mirror (press 4.24 and earlier) computes one blocked set per command (destination flags and mcp:write-flags always, root control-plane flags unless the command redefines them locally), leaves those flags out of the tool schema, and refuses both them and any argument the command does not declare with an error naming it; before, the schema advertised them, the shell-out layer forwarded any key it was handed, and blocked ones were dropped silently, so a call ran without the input it asked for and an undeclared key reached a subcommand through the args field (superops raw --vars @path) (plus 1 more, see why)
handfixes.why: The MCP server runs the companion CLI as the account that hosts it; the operator at the command line is trusted, an MCP caller is not. tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py derives, from data flow in this connector's code, every flag whose value can start a filesystem path (open, read, write, stat, mkdir, walk, exec, @path expansion), then drives the real MCP server and asserts each such flag is absent from every mirrored tool's schema and refused by name when supplied, and that an ordinary flag still reaches the CLI. On origin/main this connector failed it. Edits: the cobratree mirror (press 4.24 and earlier) computes one blocked set per command (destination flags and mcp:write-flags always, root control-plane flags unless the command redefines them locally), leaves those flags out of the tool schema, and refuses both them and any argument the command does not declare with an error naming it; before, the schema advertised them, the shell-out layer forwarded any key it was handed, and blocked ones were dropped silently, so a call ran without the input it asked for and an undeclared key reached a subcommand through the args field (superops raw --vars @path); `raw query` and `raw mutation` declare --vars inline-only, so over MCP it accepts an inline JSON object and refuses an @path value by name. The CLI keeps every flag. A reprint that drops these edits fails that check in CI and these asserts here. The args field also refuses an @path positional on raw query/mutation only (they resolve @file by reading it; elsewhere @Acme is an ordinary name); the GraphQL document is passed inline over MCP.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: derive the MCP-refused flag set from data flow (a flag whose value can start a filesystem path) instead of usage text or a name list, drop refused flags from every tool schema, refuse them by name at call time, and refuse binary multipart fields in the in-process endpoint handler. Drafted as an upstream issue for cli-printing-press (import --input exposure); tools/maintainer/check_mcp_file_flags.py is the fleet gate until a reprint carries it.

handfixes.why: SuperOps list queries return listInfo{hasMore} and page by `page`; the generated GraphQL sync read only Relay pageInfo, so every resource stored its first 50 rows and reported complete.

handfixes.why: The generated sync failed every resource under --dry-run (missing_connection, exit 1).

handfixes.summary: Every SuperOps resource is keyed on its vendor id (spec id_field, store.go resourceIDFieldOverrides) and all 14 are in the default sync set.
handfixes.why: With no declared key the store keyed several resources on name or a content fingerprint, so distinct records collapsed into one row; six resources were missing from the default sync set, so the local novels read empty tables. The spec id_field survives a reprint; the asserts pin the result.

handfixes.why: raw query is read-only on MCP but forwarded any document, mutations included, and raw mutation sent live without confirmation.

handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 has mcp:write-positionals but no read form, so raw query @/path over MCP read a file on the server's host.

handfixes.summary: The local store and sync checkpoint are scoped to credential + CustomerSubDomain + base URL; a pre-tenant store (credential-only data-<hash>.db or a 4.24 data.db) is never adopted, so an upgrade starts a fresh store. A store also records its tenant (subdomain and base URL, never a credential) in the superops_store_tenant table, and every open of the store, read-only or read-write, CLI or MCP, goes through one check (store.enforceStoreTenant, called from OpenReadOnlyContext and OpenWithContext): a store of another tenant is refused, and a store that records no tenant is never read: a read-only open refuses it whether or not it holds data (TenantRefusal.Unclaimed names sync with the same --db), an open whose tenant is unknown refuses it, and only a read-write open claims it (store.claimTenant), on one connection inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE, and only when no table in sqlite_master other than SQLite's own and the tenant record holds a row (storeHoldsRows: synced, checkpoint, FTS and shadow, learn and any later table), so the check and the record are one write-locked step and two first opens give one owner. The tenant comes from one configuration snapshot per run (cli.runSnapshot: one per command execution, started in the root pre-run, and one per MCP sql/search tool call via cli.MCPStoreRun): the default-store scope, rootFlags.newClient and doctor read the same *config.Config, and every store open carries the run's tenant in its context (store.WithTenantSource), so the store is checked against and recorded for the tenant the client sends. The response cache key folds CustomerSubDomain.
handfixes.why: The tenant is the CustomerSubDomain header plus the host; neither keyed the store or the checkpoint, so tenant B resumed tenant A's cursor and read A's rows, and an upgrade could adopt a store of unknown tenant. The scoped default path kept the default store apart, but the store file recorded no tenant, so any other route to a store mixed tenants: sync --db shared.db as acme-a then acme-b left A's rows under B (Codex P1), and with no credential superops-mcp sql read a planted data.db holding A's rows (adversarial P2). Review round 2 found the first record check was check-then-act: a read-only open of an empty unrecorded store returned without claiming it, so tenant B could claim and fill the file between tenant A's open and A's query (P1); the store re-read --config at open time apart from the read the client was built from, so a config edit between the two stamped the store for B while A's rows went in (P1); and the claim checked only the synced tables, so a pre-record file holding only A's learn rows was claimed by B's first read-write open and B's recall returned A's note (P2). CustomerSubDomain matched none of the generic tenant-selecting header rules, so one token at two subdomains shared cached GET bodies.

handfixes.summary: config.SuperOpsTenant builds the tenant identity from the base URL's scheme, host, port and path only (net/url, through cliutil.URLWithoutUserinfo, the parse rule every display of a base URL shares (superops-base-url-never-printed); never userinfo, query or fragment; lowercased whole, as before, so https://api.superops.ai and https://euapi.superops.ai give the same identity as before). A base URL that does not parse or names no scheme and host gives base_url=invalid, never the raw text. So does one with an '@', in any percent encoding (%40, %2540), outside the userinfo the parser separates (cliutil.URLUserinfoDisplaced): a username or password with an unescaped '/', '?' or '#', or an escaped '@', is otherwise read as the host, port, path, query or fragment, which the identity keeps. The identity is the one source of the store tenant record, the sync checkpoint scope key and the default store path hash. The tenant record carries a version (2); a version 1 record (the whole base URL) of the running tenant is rewritten with every checkpoint scope key in one transaction by a read-write open (secure_delete on, then a TRUNCATE WAL checkpoint, so no old page survives), a read-only open refuses it (TenantRefusal.Unscrubbed) without printing it, and a version 1 record of another tenant is refused and left alone.
handfixes.why: The identity kept the raw base URL, lowercased, so SUPEROPS_BASE_URL=http://svc:PASSWORD@host wrote the password into superops_store_tenant on any read-write open (even learnings list) and into sync_state.scope_key after a sync, and the MCP sql tool read both back (adversarial round 2, P1). The client already treats URL userinfo as a credential. A reprint regenerates the generated store and client but not these hand files; this entry pins the sanitizing line, the version bump, the scrub and its tests so a merge that brings back the raw URL fails CI.

handfixes.summary: A username or password in SUPEROPS_BASE_URL (URL userinfo, http://user:password@host) is never shown in any output: stdout, stderr, --json/--agent envelopes, doctor (human and JSON), --dry-run previews, retry notices, error messages, sync events, the jobs ledger, MCP tool results and MCP errors. One helper, cliutil.DisplayURL (internal/cliutil/url_redact.go), shows a URL as scheme://host[:port]/path through cliutil.URLWithoutUserinfo, the same parse rule the tenant identity uses: never the userinfo, the query or the fragment (nothing shows those are free of a credential); a URL that does not parse as scheme://host, or that parses with an '@' left in its path, query or fragment, shows as the fixed placeholder cliutil.URLWithheld. Routed through it: doctor base_url, the two untrusted-config refusals and the global-credential refusal (config.go), and the client's displayURL (dry-run and error prefixes). Backstop for text this program did not build (net/http's url.Error keeps the username; url.Parse errors quote the whole URL): cliutil.RedactURLUserinfo removes any URL's userinfo (plain, JSON \/ and percent-encoded forms) in the client's maskCredentialText, at the CLI error chokepoints (funnelError, funnelShownError, which doctor's error fields now use too) and in the MCP funnelToolErrors middleware; and the userinfo parts (password at any length, username of 8+ characters, the pair, and the HTTP Basic header built from it) are registered as credentials: masked by maskCredentialText and held by the shared funnel (config.Load, client.New, and the MCP server at start), so FunnelHeld withholds any decoded echo. A transport error that lost only userinfo keeps its error chain (urlRedactedError), so timeouts and refused connections still classify; a request parse error is masked and does not unwrap. The jobs ledger records and shows wait errors without userinfo. The backstop for error text the program does not construct lives in superops-owned files (internal/cli/superops_url_redact_cli.go wrapped around every command after the shared funnel; cmd/superops-mcp/superops_url_redact_mcp.go registered inside funnelToolErrors), never in the canonical secret_funnel_*.go copies, which ship byte-identical fleet-wide. A base URL with an '@', in any percent encoding, outside the userinfo the parser separates (cliutil.URLUserinfoDisplaced: part of a username or password was read as host, port, path, query or fragment) shows as cliutil.URLWithheld, and config.Load refuses it, and a base URL with a query or fragment outside its userinfo (cliutil.URLHasQueryOrFragment: request paths are appended to the base URL, so neither can be part of a working one, and request errors quote the whole URL), in refuseUnshowableBaseURL after the env override and the tenant routing, with a message that holds none of it, so no request, preview or request error is ever built from it.
handfixes.why: The previous fix removed userinfo from what is STORED (the tenant identity); this one covers what is SHOWN. With SUPEROPS_BASE_URL=http://svc:PASSWORD@host, doctor printed base_url verbatim (human and --json), the untrusted-config and global-credential refusals printed it with %q on stderr, in doctor and auth status and as the command error, every --dry-run preview printed it in the request line, and every transport failure printed net/http's url.Error with the username (retry notices, command errors, sync events, MCP tool errors and the MCP server log); a base URL that does not parse printed the password too, and a 401 body echoing the Basic header showed the pair in base64. A reprint regenerates doctor.go, config.go, client.go and jobs.go, so this entry pins every routed call and bans the raw forms; the tests prove each output path both ways (the userinfo absent in plain, URL-escaped, base64, hex and JSON-escaped form, and the host still shown).

handfixes.summary: HTTP mode (superops-mcp --transport http) serves only behind a SUPEROPS_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN no caller can know without being given it: at least 32 characters, all of them bearer-token characters (RFC 6750 b64token: A-Z a-z 0-9 - . _ ~ + / =). requireUnguessableHTTPCallerToken (cmd/superops-mcp/superops_http_token.go) runs after the press's requireHTTPCallerToken in main.go, so an unresolved manifest placeholder (${user_config.superops_mcp_http_token}), unexpanded shell text ($(openssl rand -hex 32), $VAR) and short shared words are refused before the listener starts; the refusal never shows the token.
handfixes.why: Codex next-batch round 1: the press accepted any non-empty token, including the .mcpb manifest's literal placeholder, so a non-loopback HTTP server with TLS files could start behind a publicly known bearer token. main.go is regenerated by a reprint, so this entry pins the call; the template's own non-empty check is kept.

handfixes.summary: config.Load refuses any credential shorter than cliutil.MinDetectableSecretLen (8, the funnel's funnelMinSecretLen, equal to the client's minEncodedSecretLen): the API token, the access, refresh and client-secret fields, an auth header (and the token after its scheme), and the base URL's userinfo secret (the password, or the username when there is no password; cliutil.URLUserinfoTooShort). Since superops-credential-holder a short value is also held and withheld in every encoding (cliutil.WithholdHeld), so the floor is no longer what keeps it out of output; it stays as the refusal before anything is sent, since no SuperOps credential is that short and a short one would withhold most output. refuseUndetectableCredentials runs after refuseUnshowableBaseURL; its message names no value, and nothing is sent.
handfixes.why: Codex next-batch round 1: with SUPEROPS_BASE_URL=https://svc:pw@api.superops.ai, a GraphQL error whose message was cHc= (base64 of pw) reached raw query output, because encoded-form checks skip credentials under 8 bytes. config.go is regenerated by a reprint, so this entry pins the call, and pins the client's minEncodedSecretLen so a press change to that floor is noticed.

handfixes.summary: The CustomerSubDomain header every request sends and the tenant identity (config.SuperOpsTenant, the store stamp) come from one value. config.Load folds every [headers] spelling of CustomerSubDomain into Config.Subdomain and deletes it from Headers (unifyTenantHeader), so the client sends only the header it derives from the subdomain; a [headers] value that disagrees with the subdomain setting, or two spellings that disagree, is refused (errTenantHeaderConflict); SUPEROPS_SUBDOMAIN replaces both.
handfixes.why: Codex next-batch round 1 (class A): two private configs naming their tenant only in [headers] CustomerSubDomain had the same identity (subdomain empty), so tenant B read and synced into the store tenant A had stamped. config.go is regenerated by a reprint; this entry pins the call.

handfixes.summary: The learn journal keeps no text the operator typed in place of a declared name: the SUPEROPS_LEARN_SESSION override is stored as "o:" plus the same 64-bit SHA-256 hash the harness session ids get under "h:"; argv_shape records only flag names the invoked command declares under exactly the typed name, every other name as the "<undeclared>" placeholder (redacted), and nothing after "--"; failed_flag is never kept as typed ("--<undeclared>" when Cobra matched it to a declared flag, otherwise dropped); teach.log's missing --query lines record argument counts. Operator-named text the program persists is refused when it repeats a held credential in any form the output filter knows: the journal entry is checked whole (cliutil.HeldText) after every field is filled, timestamp and session key included; the learn tables pass the sqlite-held driver; profiles, teach.log, learnings and feedback pass their held writers (superops-credential-holder). journal_credential_hardening_test.go drives each path with a credential, not held and held, and fails if it reaches any file under the test home.
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0 (learn/journal.go.tmpl) returns the override raw from JournalSessionKey, so a credential set there is written to journal-*.jsonl on every command, version included; it records every typed flag name, so a credential typed as a flag name (or after --) becomes an argv_shape key and the failed_flag; teach.log records the raw arguments of a teach with no --query. The fleet tool for this (apply_journal_hardening.py) will not merge (owner decision 2026-10-28), so the edits are made by hand. AppendJournalEntry stays byte-identical (its annotated line keeps fleet precedent); JournalInvocation, its only caller, fills the timestamp and session key before the held check. Known limits: a guessable override can be confirmed by hashing guesses; entries an older build wrote stay until the 14-day retention deletes their segment. A reprint that drops these edits fails these asserts and TestJournalCredentialHardening.

handfixes.summary: README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json say the ChatGPT desktop app runs this connector locally (STDIO) and that ChatGPT on the web, Microsoft 365 Copilot / Copilot Studio and the Gemini app are not supported by msp-skills yet, with a link to the hosted-gateway comparison; no paid-plan list, no Developer Mode recipe, no 'ChatGPT connects only to remote servers'.

OpenAI's MCP docs (https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/extend/mcp) say the ChatGPT desktop app, Codex CLI and the IDE extension support MCP servers, add them as STDIO, and share MCP configuration; ChatGPT on the web uses remote MCP through plugins and does not read local Codex config. The old text listed ChatGPT plans, said ChatGPT connects only to remote servers, and on the reprinted connectors told users to host the connector over HTTPS for a Developer Mode connector and Copilot Studio; SECURITY.md pauses HTTP mode until each connector is reprinted. README.md, mcp-install.md and page.json are regenerated by msp-skills-publish onboard.py, whose template still writes the old ChatGPT text, so without this entry a re-onboard or reprint silently restores it.
